name: Hyperion JV (Meta / Blue Owl — Beignet Investor LLC)
monetization: Bankruptcy-remote joint venture that owns Meta's Hyperion data-center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana; monetizes via Meta's lease payments, which service $27.3B of amortizing A+ notes — Meta's largest capex project, moved off its balance sheet.
description_md: The Hyperion JV is the October 2025 joint venture between Meta (20%) and funds managed by Blue Owl Capital (80%) that owns and develops the Hyperion AI data-center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana — Meta's largest data-center project. It was financed through Beignet Investor LLC, a bankruptcy-remote SPV that issued a single $27.294B 144A-for-life senior secured, fully amortizing bond, priced at par on October 16, 2025 with a 6.581% fixed coupon (reported ~+225bp over Treasuries), quarterly pay, expected final maturity May 30, 2049, rated A+ by S&P — one notch below Meta's own rating. Roughly $2.5B of JV equity sits beneath the notes, and Meta received a one-time distribution of ~$3B at close. PIMCO anchored the bond with ~$18B; BlackRock took >$3B.
ai_monetization_md: Cash flows in from one source: Meta's lease commitments for the campus, which service the notes. Two-sided accounting: Meta treats the JV as an unconsolidated variable-interest entity (Meta is not deemed the primary beneficiary), so neither the $27B+ of debt nor the assets appear on Meta's balance sheet — Meta records its 20% under the equity method plus lease obligations as they arise. The JV/noteholders' protection is structural: senior security over the campus, full amortization, and a Meta residual-value guarantee for the first 16 years of operations — a capped cash payment based on the campus's then-current value if leases are not renewed or are terminated under certain conditions. The ~$3B distribution to Meta at close means Meta extracted cash up front while retaining operational use of the asset.
risk_notes_md: The consolidation judgment is the central controversy (`spv_shift` pattern): in February 2026, auditor EY flagged Meta's off-balance-sheet treatment of the JV as a critical audit matter, citing the high degree of judgment in concluding Meta is not the primary beneficiary — reported by WSJ and others. Economically, noteholders hold 24-year paper against a single-tenant, purpose-built AI campus: if Meta walked at a renewal window after year 16, there is no residual-value guarantee left and no obvious alternative tenant at scale. The structure is also the template being copied (El Paso at 7.53% in Jul 2026), so its performance sets the market's price for all hyperscaler SPV paper.

Total financing ~$30B = $27.3B notes + ~$2.5B equity; Blue Owl funds hold 80% of JV equity, Meta 20%.

observations.notes: Meta received ~$3B cash while keeping 20% ownership and sole-tenant use — the feature bear analysts cite as capex-for-cash financial engineering.

events.title: Beignet Investor LLC prices $27.294B senior secured notes at 6.581%
events.why_it_matters: Largest private-placement data-center bond ever; created the off-balance-sheet template (lease + residual-value guarantee + SPV notes) for the rest of the cycle.

events.title: EY flags Hyperion off-balance-sheet treatment as a critical audit matter
events.why_it_matters: Meta's own auditor publicly marked the consolidation judgment — whether Meta is the primary beneficiary of a $27B+ vehicle it uses exclusively — as high-risk, the sharpest official challenge yet to AI SPV accounting.
